title: C482/1425/2023 of HERA SHAUHARAT Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
C482 1425 of 2023
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Dr. Kartikey Hari Gupta, Advocate, for the
applicant.
Mr. Tumul Nainwal, Brief Holder, for the
State of Uttarakhand.
The treatise of this C-482 Application is an
attempt by the applicant to mislead the Court, so
that due to paucity of time with the Court, at the
hearing at admission stage, the entire document
may not be diligently gone into by the Court, and
the Court may interfere at an interim stage.
The learned counsel for the applicant has
argued that based upon the documents, the contents
of the FIR, and also report, which has been heavily
relied upon, being the report dated 28th September,
2021, that the allegation levelled by the
complainant/respondent is an absurdity.
The absurdity is a very vague connotation,
which cannot be culled out merely because of
reading of the document until and unless its
intention is established during trial by leading
evidence.
The jurisdiction under Section 482 of the
Cr.P.C. by the High Court cannot be permitted to be
mis-utilized and widened to an extent, as if the
applicant approaching the Court and arguing the

matter, as if trial is being conducted, or mini trial is
required to be conducted by appreciation of
evidence.
Even if the FIR and the summoning order are
taken into consideration, as far as the applicant is
concerned, against whom the set of allegation was
found to be established as per the observation made
in the chargesheet submitted by the Investigating
Officer. What gravity it holds, is a question to be
decided by the Trial Court by appreciation of the
evidence, which has been attempted to be made
before this Court by the applicant, in a proceeding
under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.
After hearing the argument of the learned
counsel for the applicant and having gone through
the records, though at this stage, it may not be
practically possible to scrutinize all CDs, which
have been annexed with the C-482 Application, for
the purposes of arriving at a conclusion whether
prima facie case is made out against the present
applicant or not. That itself would suffice, from the
contents of the chargesheet as submitted by the
Investigating Officer by observing thereof, that the
offence under Sections 323, 504 and 498-A of the
IPC, are made out against the present applicant.
Hence, this Court declines to interfere in the
C-482 Application, because it entails a prolonged
appreciation of evidence, which may not be the
scope under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.
The C-482 Application is accordingly

dismissed, without prejudice to the rights of the
applicant to resort to the recourses as provided by
the Hon'ble Apex Court in the matter of Satender
Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of
Investigation and another as reported in (2022) 10
SCC 51.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
Dated 18.07.2023
Shiv
